## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable codes: Signal domain failures by raising ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a short snake_case code (e.g. "invalid_state", "invalid_quantity", "negative_amount") and a repr/detail string, matching existing invoice.py functions.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 1 passed, 2 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary Decimal results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0004] Reject bools in integer validation: When validating integer fields, exclude bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since True/False pass isinstance(int).

- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 require approved_by: Support-initiated refunds/credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Record audit entry for every money movement: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...) against the entity the money moves on. Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries, so never mutate payment/invoice state without one.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize unit prices with to_money: Wrap raw line unit prices with ledgerly.money.to_money before arithmetic, and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do.
